title: Parity of the Trigonometric Function f(x) = sin(2x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the trigonometric function f(x) = sin(2x) is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Substitute -x into the Function
steps.explanation: Replace x with -x in the argument of the sine function.
steps.why: Parity is determined by comparing the value at -x with the value at x.

steps.title: Apply the Odd Identity of the Sine Function
steps.explanation: Because the sine function satisfies the fundamental trigonometric identity sin(-theta) = -sin(theta) for all real angles theta, setting theta = 2x gives sin(-2x) = -sin(2x).
steps.why: On the unit circle, reflecting an angle theta to -theta reflects the y-coordinate sin(theta) to -sin(theta).

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Since f(-x) = -f(x) for all real x, f(x) = sin(2x) is an odd function.
steps.why: Composing an odd function (sin u) with an odd linear scaling (u = 2x) yields an odd function.
